help.intro: A scene of about one and a half minutes in a flat on a Monday morning: Jonas is late and cannot find his key, his phone, his glasses or his bag, and his flatmate Sara tells him where everything is. The scene is invented. You hear what you have just learnt: Wo ist …? with the answers in, auf, unter, neben, hinter, vor + the dative (auf dem Tisch, in der Küche, unter dem Sofa), and verbs with a vowel change (du siehst, er sieht, du nimmst, er isst). Listen once for the whole scene, then once per object: where is it in the end?
help.tips[0].text: The question Wo? (where) gets an answer with a preposition and the dative: der Tisch → auf dem Tisch; das Sofa → unter dem Sofa; die Küche → in der Küche; die Tasche → in der Tasche. In short: der and das become dem, die becomes der. in dem is usually im: im Bad, im Kühlschrank. The prepositions: in (in), auf (on top of), unter (under), neben (next to), hinter (behind), vor (in front of), zwischen (between).
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: Where is the key? It is lying on the table, next to the newspaper.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: Where are the glasses? They are in the bathroom, in front of the mirror.
help.tips[0].check.q: Wo ist das Handy? Es ist ____ Sofa.
help.tips[0].check.why: Wo? takes the dative; das Sofa → dem Sofa.
help.tips[1].title: Verbs that change their vowel
help.tips[1].text: Some verbs change e → ie / i or a → ä only for du and er/sie/es: sehen: ich sehe, du siehst, er sieht. nehmen: ich nehme, du nimmst, er nimmt. essen: ich esse, du isst, er isst. fahren: ich fahre, du fährst, er fährt. schlafen: du schläfst, er schläft. The wir, ihr and sie forms keep the normal vowel: wir sehen, ihr nehmt.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: Do you see my glasses? No, I do not see them.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: You take the bus at eight, and it leaves at five past eight.
help.tips[1].check.why: essen changes e → i for du and er: er isst (spelled with ss since the reform).
help.remember[0]: Wo? → dative: auf dem Tisch, unter dem Sofa, in der Küche, im Bad.
help.remember[1]: du siehst / er sieht, du nimmst / er nimmt, du isst / er isst, er fährt.
help.exam: Short everyday scenes in which you have to hear where things are are a typical listening task at this level.
help.hook: Monday, 7:50, and Jonas cannot find his key, his phone or his glasses. Listen to where everything really is.
passageTranslation:
Jonas: Sara! It is ten to eight! Where is my key?
Sara: Good morning, Jonas. Your key is in the kitchen, on the table. Next to the coffee cup.
Jonas: Ah, yes. Thanks. And my phone? Do you see my phone?
Sara: No, I do not see it. Is it in the bathroom?
Jonas: No, it is not in the bathroom.
Sara: Then it is under the sofa. Your phone is always under the sofa.
Jonas: Yes! Here it is. Under the sofa. And my glasses?
Sara: Jonas, your glasses are on your head.
Jonas: Oh. Okay. And my bag?
Sara: The bag is behind the door, in the hall. Between the shoes and the umbrella.
Jonas: Behind the door. Good. Do I have everything? Key, phone, glasses, bag.
Sara: You are taking the bus at eight?
Jonas: Yes, the bus leaves at five past eight.
Sara: Then you still have ten minutes. Are you eating a sandwich?
Jonas: No, I will eat on the bus. Bye, Sara! Thanks!
Sara: Jonas! Your jacket! It is here, in front of you, on the chair!
Jonas: Oh no. Thanks. Now I really have everything. See you tonight!
